paper_title: 1+12 Can Large Language Models Serve as Cross-Lingual Knowledge   Aggregators
caption: Statistics of the dataset in our experiments.
model_annotation: The figure is a 3D pie chart summarizing the composition of the dataset used in the experiments, showing 5 labeled categories (slices) with percentages and sample counts printed directly next to the corresponding wedges. The slices are: TriviaQA in red at about 46% (1829), WebQA in purple at about 25% (997), HalluEval in green at about 18% (721), Chinese Domain in yellow at about 6% (231), and HalluQA in light blue at about 5% (185). There is no separate legend; instead, each slice is annotated with its label and “% (count)” text. Several wedges appear visually offset (“exploded”) from the center—most noticeably the large red TriviaQA slice and the yellow Chinese Domain slice (and the green slice appears slightly separated as well). The slice sizes appear arranged roughly from largest to smaller categories around the pie, as seen from the 46% segment down to the 5% segment.
